shipped_rows.title_o: A Metacontingency Experiment: The Effects of Contingent Consequences on Patterns of Interlocking Contingencies of Reinforcement
shipped_rows.outcome_quote: Controlling relations between cultural consequences and the behavior of dividing were statistically significant in one of the groups, whereas in the other two groups controlling relations were observed only in Contingency B.

prior_scientific_decisions.quote: If, as in Vichi et al (2009) and Lopes (2010), the study considers only if successive gains reached the criterion for contingency change, then we can state that the data here obtained replicated the ones from Vichi et al. and disagree with the ones from Lopes, since all groups reached these criteria. In this sense, the contingencies here manipulated established control over collective behaviors, being an experimental analogous to metacontingencies.
prior_scientific_decisions.reason: Under the original study's criterion for contingency control (reaching the successive-gains criterion for contingency change), the authors explicitly state that all three groups replicated Vichi et al. (2009) and established control over collective behaviors. While the authors also conduct an additional binomial statistical test showing significance in both contingencies only for G1 and only under Contingency B for G2 and G3, they explicitly state in the Discussion (lines 642-644) that because Vichi et al. (2009) did not conduct that statistical treatment, the comparison cannot be made, and they do not argue that the original method is invalid as a test of the hypothesis.
